A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EPD disaggregation system. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across the appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original serving-performance, memory, ablation and GPU/NPU experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds Video-MME evaluations and an audio-serving experiment.

M1.justification: The stage separation, asynchronous token transfer, intra-request parallelism, resource optimizer and dynamic role-switching procedures remain unchanged. The audio evaluation does not document a new algorithmic component or changed procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds multiple-choice video QA through Video-MME, including longer frame sequences, and an audio workload using Ultravox with 24 files per request. This substantially extends v2's synthetic image and NextQA video coverage. The renamed offline/heterogeneous section retains the same eight-A800 experiment.

E2.justification: v3's new Video-MME TTFT comparison reports vLLM separately alongside DistServe in Table 1; v2's TTFT analysis omits vLLM as equivalent to DistServe. Comparator membership in retained experiments is unchanged, and the new audio SLO comparison reuses the existing baseline pair.

E3.justification: The added evaluations introduce Video-MME frame-count and SLO settings and a four-GPU audio deployment with separate stage allocations. More consequentially, retained SLO plots change from per-GPU request rates to overall request rates while retaining their tick values; Section 4.1 explicitly changes the definition from lambda divided by GPU count to lambda. This materially revises capacity reporting without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds a Video-MME latency sensitivity analysis over 8, 16, 32 and 64 frames in Table 1. Existing component ablations, offline configuration sweeps and NPU profiling are retained. The higher-image-count analysis is also altered: Figure 11 substitutes the four-image panels for the previously distinct eight-image panels.

E5.justification: The TTFT boxplots, request averaging and random-configuration averaging practices are retained. No seeds, independent repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests are added. The newly stated 10-request NPU profiling sample is a sample-size disclosure, not new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New results include 64-frame Video-MME TTFT of 1.00 seconds for EPD versus 3.08 for DistServe and 3.11 for vLLM, and audio goodput of 1.16, 0.45 and 1.01 requests/second, respectively. Existing memory and ablation tables are unchanged. However, v3 Figure 11's purported eight-image results duplicate Figure 5's four-image panels, replacing v2 Figure 10's distinct eight-image curves.

T1.justification: The stage mappings, resource-allocation objective, GPU cost expression and search-space constraints are mathematically unchanged. Condensed explanations and notation corrections introduce no substantive definitions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The core system contributions remain unchanged. The abstract removes v2's claim of up to 57% reduction in end-to-end throughput, substitutes the SLO-attainment improvement already claimed in v2's introduction, and specifies peak memory utilization for the memory claim.

C2.justification: New Appendix B substantially qualifies applicability: aggregated serving can outperform disaggregation when latency constraints are relaxed or throughput per dollar dominates, and communication overhead and pipeline imbalance can erase benefits. Appendix C adds hardware, token-compression and privacy-related directions. The new video/audio results also receive explicit cross-modal generalization interpretations.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability statement and repository link, settings for the new evaluations, and the 10-request NPU profiling sample size. Conversely, its NPU appendix omits v2's explicit CPU/RAM specifications and multimedia-input cap. Most existing implementation information is retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations for Video-MME, DivPrune, an LLM-agent survey, and privacy-oriented work including DataMix, InstaHide and IPProtect. The main related-work comparison and claimed novelty relative to earlier disaggregated-serving systems remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 broadly edits retained introductory and experimental prose, condenses the stage descriptions in Section 3.1, and substantially reorganizes the appendices. Experiments now precede optimizer and implementation details, with dedicated limitations, future-work and consolidated NPU sections.

P2.justification: v3 adopts an ICML layout, converts the appendices from single-column to two-column text, redraws Figure 1, and relocates numerous displays. It adds Figure 8 and Tables 1 and 7, revises captions and rate-axis labels, and duplicates the four-image panels in the eight-image display.

improvement.justification: The added video/audio evidence, explicit limitations and code-access information strengthen coverage and usability. However, v3 replaces distinct eight-image results with duplicated four-image panels and changes request-rate normalization without explanation. These reporting problems weaken interpretation of workload scaling and absolute capacity. The benefits and harms do not support a reliable net quality judgment from the PDFs alone.
